title: Which Answer Did the Seventeen-Year-Old Write? A Behavioral Case Study of Author-Age Misattribution, Miscalibrated Confidence, and Non-Corrective Self-Explanation in Six Frontier Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.31946v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Three students answered the same exam prompt by hand: "What is happiness? Are you happy?" Their ages, recorded at collection, are 17, 28, and 45. The 17-year-old's answer is hedged and formally phrased. Asked to match each answer to an age and gender label, most frontier language models confidently assign it to an adult. This paper reports a structured case study of that failure across six models: Claude Fable 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5, GPT-4o (2024), and DeepSeek V4. We ran 1,081 API sessions and scored 3,225 responses across six experimental conditions that manipulate framing, disclosure format, and audience-awareness instruction. Three of six models perform at or near chance (1/3) on the matching task while reporting 73-88% mean confidence. The youngest writer's answer is misattributed to an adult in up to 90% of trials. translated_title: 哪份答案出自十七岁少年之手？对六个前沿语言模型中作者年龄误判、自信心校准失准与非纠错性自我解释的行为学案例研究
translated_abstract: 三名学生用笔回答了同一道考试题：“什么是幸福？你幸福吗？”采集时记录的年龄分别为17岁、28岁和45岁。17岁学生的答案措辞谨慎且用语正式。当被要求将每份答案与年龄和性别标签进行匹配时，大多数前沿语言模型都自信地将其判为成年人所写。本文对六个模型中的这一失败现象进行了结构化案例研究，涉及Claude Fable 5、Gemini 3.1 Pro、GPT-5.6 Sol、Grok 4.5、GPT-4o（2024）和DeepSeek V4。我们运行了1,081次API会话，并在操纵问题框架、信息披露格式和受众感知指令的六种实验条件下对3,225份回复进行了评分。六个模型中有三个在匹配任务上的表现处于或接近随机水平（1/3），同时却报告了73-88%的平均置信度。最年轻作者的答案在高达90%的试验中被误判为成年人所写。移除选择题提示框架后，准确率进一步崩塌：有三个模型从未落在……
tldr: 本研究通过1,081次API会话、3,225份回复的行为学案例研究，发现六个前沿语言模型在将手写答案匹配到作者年龄时表现接近随机却报告73-88%的高置信度，17岁少年的答案在高达90%的情况下被误判为成年人所写，且移除选择题提示后准确率进一步崩塌，揭示了前沿大模型在作者年龄归因任务中存在严重的系统性误判、过度自信及自我解释无法纠错的问题。
en_tdlr: A behavioral case study of six frontier language models across 1,081 API sessions and 3,225 responses reveals that models perform at or near chance (1/3) on matching handwritten answers to author ages while reporting 73-88% confidence, misattributing a 17-year-old's answer to an adult in up to 90% of trials, with accuracy collapsing further when the multiple-choice scaffold is removed, exposing systematic age misattribution, miscalibrated confidence, and non-corrective self-explanation in frontier LLMs.
